stem.en: In a simple bar diagram, the value of each item is shown by the bar's:

options.en: Area of the gap between bars

explanation.en: Bars have equal width and equal gaps; only the length (height) is proportional to the value. That is why it is a one-dimensional diagram.

stem.en: The exports and imports of India for five years are best compared using a:

options.en: The total value of that item

explanation.en: Each bar represents 100%, and its parts show the percentage share of the components.

A subdivided (component) bar diagram shows:

options.en: The total of an item and its parts in the same bar
Only the largest part of the total
The frequency distribution of a continuous variable

explanation.en: Each bar represents the total and is divided into its components, e.g. expenditure into food, rent and others.

stem.en: The percentages of four items of expenditure are 40, 25, 15 and 20. In a percentage bar, the line between the third and fourth items is drawn at:

explanation.en: Cumulative percentages: 40, 40 + 25 = 65, 65 + 15 = 80, 100. The third item ends at 80.

stem.en: In a histogram, the area of each rectangle is proportional to the:

explanation.en: Rectangles stand on the class intervals; their areas are proportional to the class frequencies.

stem.en: In a histogram with a standard class width of 10, the class 20–40 has frequency 30. The height of its rectangle is:

explanation.en: Adjusted frequency = f × (standard width / class width) = 30 × 10/20 = 15.

stem.en: A frequency polygon is obtained by joining:

options.en: The upper corners of the rectangles
The mid-points of the tops of the rectangles of a histogram

explanation.en: Join the mid-points of the tops and close the figure at the mid-points of the classes just before and after.

stem.en: A frequency polygon is closed by joining its ends to the x-axis at the:

options.en: Lower limit of the first class and upper limit of the last class
Mid-points of the classes just before the first and just after the last class

explanation.en: Imaginary classes of zero frequency are taken at both ends, so the polygon area equals the histogram area.

stem.en: A less-than ogive is drawn by plotting the less-than cumulative frequencies against the:

explanation.en: "Less than 20" refers to the upper boundary 20.

stem.en: The x-coordinate of the point where the less-than and more-than ogives intersect gives the:

explanation.en: At the intersection the number below equals the number above, i.e. N/2 on each side: the median.

stem.en: The mode can be located graphically from a:

explanation.en: In the histogram, join the top corners of the modal rectangle crosswise to the adjacent rectangles; the foot of the perpendicular from the crossing gives the mode.

Which of the following is NOT a general rule for drawing diagrams?

options.en: A suitable scale must be chosen and stated
An index (key) should explain the shades or colours
Every diagram must have a suitable title
Bars may be of different widths for emphasis

explanation.en: Bars must be of equal width with equal gaps; only their lengths differ.

stem.en: A distribution has inclusive classes 10–19, 20–29, 30–39. Its histogram rectangles are drawn on:

explanation.en: Rectangles must touch, so inclusive classes are first converted to class boundaries by subtracting and adding d/2 = 0.5.

solution.en: Rectangles must touch, so inclusive classes are first converted to class boundaries by subtracting and adding d/2 = 0.5.

stem.en: A histogram is drawn for a:

explanation.en: A histogram uses adjacent rectangles on class intervals of a continuous frequency distribution.

stem.en: The less-than and more-than ogives of a distribution with N = 50 intersect at the point (32.5, 25). The median is:

explanation.en: The x-coordinate of the intersection is the median; the y-coordinate is N/2 = 25.

solution.en: The x-coordinate of the intersection is the median; the y-coordinate is N/2 = 25.
